what_it_adds: A new 54-card deck you use instead of the base deck. Cards give new lasting powers.
what_it_fixes: Replaces some base cards that many players felt were unbalanced.
verdict_reason: Cheap and easy to add. The reviewer says every Root owner should have it.
notes: ASIN from Meeple Mountain amazon.com/dp link titled "Leder Games | Root: The Exiles and Partisans Deck".

what_it_adds: Two new factions (Riverfolk Company, Lizard Cult), three new Vagabonds, a second Vagabond and a simple bot.
what_it_fixes: Lets you play with up to 6 players and gives 4-player groups more variety.
verdict_reason: Great if you like trading and table talk, or often teach new players.
notes: Its bot (Mechanical Marquise) is superseded by Clockwork per MM. Audit: buy_order made distinct; MM does not rank faction boxes or hireling packs, so order within those groups is an owner tie-break (MM guide order / Marauder box first because it stores all hirelings).

what_it_adds: Two new factions (Underground Duchy, Corvid Conspiracy) and a new two-sided board with Mountain and Lake maps.
what_it_fixes: New maps change up the board so games feel fresh.
verdict_reason: Good for players who like flexible plans, sneaky bluffing, or new maps.
notes: First printing has correction stickers on Leder site. Audit: buy_order made distinct; MM does not rank faction boxes or hireling packs, so order within those groups is an owner tie-break (MM guide order / Marauder box first because it stores all hirelings).

what_it_adds: Two new factions (Lord of the Hundreds, Keepers in Iron), four hirelings and a new setup draft.
what_it_fixes: Makes 2- and 3-player games feel busier and more alive.
verdict_reason: Best pick if you often play with 2 or 3 people. Has factions for new and skilled players.
notes: MM advises new players skip hirelings at first. Audit: buy_order made distinct; MM does not rank faction boxes or hireling packs, so order within those groups is an owner tie-break (MM guide order / Marauder box first because it stores all hirelings).

what_it_adds: Three new factions (Lilypad Diaspora, Twilight Council, Knaves of the Deepwood) and two new maps.
what_it_fixes: Makes 5- and 6-player games playable on a bigger map.
verdict_reason: The reviewer calls it the best Root expansion and the first faction box to get. Its swamp map makes 5-6 player games work.
notes: Newest box; Leder nav still labels it "Coming Soon" though the product page shows price and Add to Cart. No review consensus found. Audit: verdict from MM review (2026-08-01); only one review found, owner to confirm. Supersedes 'no review' note.

prerequisite_rule: You need Root. You do not need the matching faction box.
what_it_adds: Small side factions that any player can control for a while.
what_it_fixes: Fills the map in small games so 2- and 3-player games feel fuller.
verdict_reason: Get one if you often play with few players. Pick the pack for factions you own least.
notes: Hireling cards cannot be used with their matching faction. Audit: buy_order made distinct; MM does not rank faction boxes or hireling packs, so order within those groups is an owner tie-break (MM guide order / Marauder box first because it stores all hirelings).

what_it_adds: Three new Vagabond characters (Ronin, Adventurer, Harrier) and seven matching Vagabond pieces.
what_it_fixes: Gives each Vagabond its own matching piece.
verdict_reason: For people who love playing the Vagabond or want matching pieces.

what_it_adds: Another swap-in deck with cards inspired by the Marauder and Homeland factions.
notes: No review consensus found. Audit: still no review found; verdict left blank.

what_it_adds: Bot versions of the four base factions for solo, co-op or filling empty seats. Three difficulty levels each.
what_it_fixes: Lets you play Root alone or with too few people.
verdict_reason: Only if you have no one to play with and do not want the digital app.
notes: Product page showed NOTIFY WHEN AVAILABLE (possibly out of stock).

prerequisite_rule: You need Root plus The Riverfolk Expansion or The Underworld Expansion (or both).
what_it_adds: Bots for the Riverfolk, Lizard, Corvid and Duchy factions, plus a new trait card for each first Clockwork bot.
what_it_fixes: Lets you play expansion factions against bots.
verdict_reason: Only for solo players or collectors who already own Riverfolk or Underworld.
notes: requires_also left blank because the need is either Riverfolk OR Underworld (not both). ASIN from MM amazon.com/dp link titled "Root: The Clockwork 2 Expansion".

what_it_adds: Four wooden landmarks you place on the map: Black Market, Lost City, Legendary Forge, Elder Treetop.
verdict_reason: Easy to add but changes little. For collectors or as a small treat.

prerequisite_rule: You need Scythe. Invaders from Afar is optional and raises the player count.
what_it_adds: An 8-game story campaign you can reset, plus 11 modules (including a co-op mode) to mix into normal games.
what_it_fixes: Keeps the game fresh for groups who have played base Scythe a lot.
verdict_reason: The one to buy first for most groups. Play the campaign, then keep using the modules.
notes: 1-5 players with base Scythe; 1-7 if you also own Invaders from Afar (publisher). IGN lists MSRP $60 vs publisher store $49 - used store price. ASIN from BGG amazon.com/dp affiliate link labelled "Scythe: The Rise of Fenris".

what_it_adds: Airships (7 big minis, 16 ability tiles) and 8 Resolution tiles that change how the game ends. Solo Automa parts too.
what_it_fixes: New end-game goals stop games from feeling the same every time.
verdict_reason: Good for groups who know the base game well and want variety without a campaign.
notes: Players 1-5 from IGN. Dice Drop says Wind Gambit includes a modular board - publisher page does NOT; the Modular Board is a separate product.

what_it_adds: Two new factions (Albion, Togawa) with 10 minis, plus two player mats that raise the max to 7 players.
what_it_fixes: Lets 6 or 7 people play and adds more faction matchups.
verdict_reason: Get it if you often have 6-7 players or want more factions. Otherwise it can wait.
notes: Sources disagree: IGN and one BGG poster say add it first; Dice Drop ranks it last ("borderline skip").

what_it_adds: A new two-sided board with 4 two-sided tiles and home base tiles, so the map changes every game.
what_it_fixes: Adds a tighter map for low player counts and stops set openings from repeating.
verdict_reason: For groups who feel their openings have become scripted.
notes: Weak consensus (single BGG thread). BGG posters say it is generally not used with the Fenris campaign.

what_it_adds: Two new Spirits, a new Adversary (France), and Event cards added to the Invader phase. Also new tokens.
what_it_fixes: Makes the island feel more alive and less predictable.
verdict_reason: Small, cheap first step. Adds events and tokens without overwhelming you.
notes: Publisher page showed Sold out on 2026-09-27.

prerequisite_rule: You need Spirit Island. Branch & Claw is not required.
what_it_adds: Ten new Spirits, more Adversaries, and parts for up to 6 players. A very big box.
what_it_fixes: Lets 5 or 6 people play and adds lots of Spirit variety.
verdict_reason: Best value if you play often. Big and more complex, so many get it second.
notes: Publisher page showed Sold out on 2026-09-27; a BGG post says it was back in US stock 2025-09-04.

what_it_adds: Four Spirits, 5 Aspects, 5 Fear cards, 2 Scenarios and 1 Adversary. Collects Promo Packs 1 and 2.
what_it_fixes: Adds new Spirits without many new rules.
verdict_reason: Can be added any time. Good if you want more Spirits but not more rules.
notes: Do not buy separately with Promo Pack 1/2 - same content. Its Spirits are high complexity per BGG.

prerequisite_rule: You need Spirit Island and Jagged Earth.
what_it_adds: Eight new Spirits and many new Aspects that change older Spirits.
verdict_reason: Get it last. It needs Jagged Earth and has the hardest Spirits.
notes: Common trap: buyers miss that Jagged Earth is required (BGG). Publisher page showed Sold out 2026-09-27. ASIN from BGG amazon.com/dp affiliate link labelled "Spirit Island: Nature Incarnate".

prerequisite_rule: Plays on its own. Also works with other Spirit Island products.
what_it_adds: A simpler standalone Spirit Island with five new Spirits that also mix into the full game.
what_it_fixes: Gives new players easier, more forgiving Spirits.
verdict_reason: Best as a cheaper, gentler way into Spirit Island. If you own the full game, it is mainly five easy Spirits to mix in.
notes: Standalone: 1-3 players on its own. No expansion-order consensus fetched. Audit: MM review rates it great as an entry point; BGG thread poster suggests buying it alongside expansions. No source ranks it against expansions.
